newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian minister-energy cost should promote growth.
newsitem.headline: Russian minister-energy cost should promote growth.

text.p: Russia's energy minister called for lower energy prices to promote growth in domestic industry in an interview with a Russian newspaper published on Thursday.

"The fuel and energy ministry should conduct tariff policies in such a way that prices of the fuel and energy complex stimulate economic growth," Fuel and Energy Minister Pyotr Rodionov told Nezavisimaya Gazeta.
"Without question the general price level of all fuel and energy resources needs to be decreased," said Rodionov, 45, who was appointed to his post by President Boris Yeltsin in August.
He was speaking in terms of prices for industry, not consumers.
"We have already given first deputy prime minister Alexei Bolshakov such a proposal from several government departments and companies," he said.
"The proposal was at the fuel and energy ministry's initiative, with the approval of the ministries of industry, railways and defence industry, RAO Gazprom and RAO Unified Energy System."
In the interview, he said that Russian domestic prices did not have to meet world level prices.
"I would especially point out that, in terms of fuel, one can never talk about abstract 'world prices' which we are urged to orient ourselves towards," he said.
Rodionov said that Russia's special circumstances called for low energy transport prices.
"Prices for energy transport should be at a level to allow (industrial) competitiveness with other countries," he said.

"Given two important objective factors -- climate conditions (in cold, northern Russia) and the size of the country -- the price of energy transport in Russia should be cheaper than in the U.S. and even Canada."
Rodionov, little known in the West, was previously head of a St Petersburg subsidiary of national gas monopoly Gazprom.
